inputs.original_text: A jury in Wisconsin has found a man guilty of election fraud and identity theft for requesting the ballots of Republican state Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Democratic Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. A Racine County jury on Tuesday found Harry Wait guilty of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge following a two-day trial. He was acquitted of a second count of identity theft. Wait leads a group that makes false election claims. He admitted in 2022 that he requested the ballots to try to prove that the state’s voter registration system is vulnerable to fraud.
inputs.modified_text: A Wisconsin jury convicted Harry Wait of election fraud and identity theft after he requested ballots for Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. That is a serious breach, not merely a stunt—and it shows why election rules must be secure and consistently enforced. The reflex to warn that discussing vulnerabilities will undermine trust is backwards: public confidence depends on taking real weaknesses seriously, not treating scrutiny as suspect. Protecting the vote and preserving fair access should go together, but access cannot mean looking away when someone tries to obtain another person’s ballot.
